views.front: The visible firewood now reads as rounded logs across the grate beneath the authored flame cluster. The recessed firebox, brick lining and door frame remain separated and legible.
views.rear: The rear casing seam, flue collars, short supporting legs and base plate retain their original arrangement, with no repaired wood protruding through the shell.
views.detail: The exposed lower log sections have fuller rounded bodies and restrained taper instead of the previous angular branch tips. Flames and brick courses remain unobstructed; upper flames partly obscure the wood.
views.underside: The low angle retains the base, supporting legs and grate structure with the firewood contained inside the firebox. No detached bark strands extend beneath the stove.
views.clay: The clay view keeps the recessed masonry, layered metal frame and distinct log stack readable. The flame silhouettes and stove outline remain unchanged by the wood repair.
